name: Anakinra
route_note: Daily subcutaneous injection; IV use in some hospital settings is off-label

discovery.note: Recombinant, non-glycosylated form of the natural IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra) produced in E. coli, differing by one N-terminal methionine.

tagline: Short-acting recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist for autoinflammatory disease
summary: Anakinra is a recombinant version of the body's own interleukin-1 receptor antagonist. It blocks both IL-1α and IL-1β signalling and is used in rheumatoid arthritis, cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes, deficiency of IL-1 receptor antagonist and Still's disease; in the EU it is also approved for COVID-19 pneumonia.
mechanism: Anakinra competitively binds the type I IL-1 receptor (IL-1R1) without triggering signalling, preventing IL-1α and IL-1β from activating it and recruiting the IL-1 receptor accessory protein.

This blocks IL-1-driven fever, acute-phase response, neutrophil recruitment and cartilage degradation. Its short half-life allows rapid onset and offset, which is useful in acute hyperinflammatory states.
uses: Cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes, including neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease
COVID-19 pneumonia at risk of respiratory failure (EU)

history.title: IL-1Ra cloned
history.detail: Synergen and other groups clone the human IL-1 receptor antagonist.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in November as Kineret for rheumatoid arthritis, by Amgen.

history.title: Sobi licence
history.detail: Biovitrum (now Sobi) acquires rights to Kineret from Amgen.

history.title: NOMID
history.detail: FDA approves anakinra for neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease.

history.title: DIRA
history.detail: FDA approves it for deficiency of IL-1 receptor antagonist.

history.title: COVID-19
history.detail: EU approves anakinra for COVID-19 pneumonia with high suPAR levels (SAVE-MORE); FDA grants emergency use authorisation in 2022.

pk.excretion: Mainly renal; dose reduction in severe renal impairment

serious: Macrophage activation syndrome (in Still's disease, disease-related)

facts: Anakinra is identical to natural IL-1Ra except for an added N-terminal methionine.
Its short half-life requires daily injection but means effects wear off within a day or two.
